9:13 Xiaomi has a Side Toolbox feature where you can open any app directly from the sidebar — not just favorites. You can also customize it to appear on the left or right side — meaning right-handed and left-handed users can both use it comfortably.
How to set it up on a fold phone (Mix Fold 3 / 18 Fold):
Settings → Special Features → Sidebar → Toggle "Always show" → Choose Left or Right → Tap "+" at the bottom to add any app (up to 10).
On fold phones, tapping an app opens it as a floating window on the inner display — you can resize, drag, or snap it into split-screen.
Also, this is an old feature — it's been around since MIUI 13 (late 2021). Phones from 5–6 years ago like Redmi Note 10 Pro, Mi 10, etc. also have it. It's not exclusive to foldables at all.

Here’s the problem. 
And this addresses some of the other comments. 

No, buying/choosing a phone purely based on benchmark scores shouldn’t be the sole reason to skip or pick it. But it can and should be a contributing factor on some level (even if it’s just a little)

The other issue is that due to the lower performance, it DEFINITELY impacts gaming on a mobile platform and this is speaking from someone who has both the 9 PXL and the 16 Pro Max. 

With the lack of performance that could also elude to a lack of efficiency. And  in this case, that’s exactly the problem. Does and can any phone heat up or over heat ? Sure! But what does it take to reach those high thermal levels? 
Since using the 16PM, the phone has only reached very warm temperatures ONCE. 
With the 9ProXL, it happened very frequently and was guaranteed to happen a couple times a week. Now, I expect, to some degree, that this will be addressed with the switch to TSMC from Samsung architecture.

And with that, thermal issues impact battery health and longevity. Internally, Google has a larger battery, by over 300 mAh - but from my day to day usage it lasts nowhere NEAR the 16PM. For example. I can use the Pixel on the same schedule as the iPhone and at around 5pm, my battery on the pixel could be at 20-30%. And the IPhone would still be rocking at 50-60% (sometimes even 70). And this is with similar usage on both phones. I’m not babying the iPhone. In fact I can use the iPhone more and it still wouldn’t drain as fast. 

So what he’s saying in the video is something I agree with. If you’re not a power user or heavy in to gaming, maybe the pixel will do okay, but even on some basic tasks and what not, Google still hasn’t solved the thermal problem and again - much of that is on Samsung’s table. And I would definitely recommend either the Galaxy or the iPhone.
